actor: Coefficient Giving (Farm Animal Welfare fund; Alternative Protein R&D RFP)
stated_interests: Funds alternative-protein R&D to close taste and price gaps: off-flavour reduction, fat alternatives, egg replacement, and characterising fish flavours in tilapia, milkfish, carp and catfish. Up to USD 30 million over two rounds (USD 0.1 to 1 million; USD 1 to 5 million), closed 10 August and 15 September 2026, decisions by 30 November and 31 December 2026. For-profits and international applicants eligible. Fund strategy includes movement building 'especially in emerging economies'. Also funded the Stanford restaurant displacement study.
key_quote: Taste and price represent the biggest barriers to mainstream adoption
vietnam_or_sea_focus: No country named. Emerging economies are a stated priority for movement building. The fish species chosen are Asian aquaculture species, including catfish (pangasius is a catfish).
demand_relevance: Medium. Asks R&D applicants for 'a credible pathway to industry uptake', so a Vietnamese applicant needs a named buyer. Demand evidence it funds is on displacement (restaurant data), which supports Part III.
notes: Grants database could not be searched from here (HTTP 403), so Vietnamese grants are unverified. Part II ch08 already covers this RFP as a supply-side grant.

stated_interests: USD 10 million RFP (grants USD 100,000 to 750,000 a year; phase 1 closed 15 September 2026; decisions late November or early December 2026) for policy (public R&D and commercialisation funding; fair, safe, fast novel-food pathways) and market shaping (public procurement of innovative protein products, advance market commitments, retailer and corporate protein-diversification commitments such as protein ratio targets, blended finance, prizes) plus experimental work (AI, open data).
key_quote: Public procurement of innovative protein products specifically.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Extra policy capacity sought in 'high-innovation Asian economies (including but not limited to Japan and South Korea), Germany at the national level, and the Nordics'. Vietnam not named.
demand_relevance: High. Defines demand evidence as institutional decisions: goals must be 'outcomes in the world' with 'an identifiable decision-maker, a reason they might move, and a window'. Out of scope: direct R&D, culture change and consumer awareness campaigns, whole-food plant-based interventions, individual diet change, and 'work whose likely effect is to shift consumption from larger animals to smaller ones'.
notes: The brief calls this the 'Nova Vista Foundation / Navigation Fund' RFP. The RFP text and announcement name only Nova Vista; we found no link to the Navigation Fund.

stated_interests: Farm animal welfare grants by invitation, three cycles a year: institutional impact (policies at food corporations, government and public institutions), movement power, target audiences, capacity building, new funding, innovation.
key_quote: Grant applications are by invitation
vietnam_or_sea_focus: No region named on the grants page. No alternative-protein RFP found, which matches Part II ch08.
demand_relevance: Low to Medium. Institutional-policy focus could cover public meals, but no demand evidence standard is published.

stated_interests: Open-access research grants (USD 27 million plus, 141 grants since 2019, 26 countries; closed in 2026, no reopening date) on organoleptic quality, cost and scale-up; 2025 round on fermentation-derived functionality and cell lines. Publishes State of the Industry market data. Advocates public R&D funding and fair labelling. Recommended by Giving Green as a top climate nonprofit.
key_quote: focused on enhancing organoleptic properties, reducing costs, and scaling up alternative proteins
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Global. Vietnam not named on the grants or State of the Industry pages. GFI's ecosystem database lists two Vietnamese companies (package ECO-22).
demand_relevance: Low for its grants (supply-side topics, no consumer research). Medium through the US and European retail data that Part III already uses.

stated_interests: Regulatory pathways, public investment, talent. 2026 watch list: Korea, Chinese biomanufacturing, climate finance, jobs narrative, 'conventional meat enhanced with plant proteins' rolled out in foodservice first at price parity, and 'protein maximisation' positioning. Ran the Decoding Demand survey (2023, Vietnam n = 1,049) and the A*STAR blended-meat taste test.
key_quote: Asia's first large-scale rollouts (of meat enhanced with plant proteins)
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines, China, Korea named. Vietnam not named in the 2025 report card; no team member listed for Vietnam.
demand_relevance: High. Produces the consumer numbers funders quote for Vietnam, and is steering corporates towards blended meat, which Part III identifies as the entry route.

actor: GFI India with the Observer Research Foundation (state feeding schemes roundtable)
stated_interests: Building plant-based and biomass-fermented proteins from local pulses, millets, oilseed meals and broken grains into PM-POSHAN school meals and ICDS take-home rations; protein quality, safety and allergenicity studies, community acceptability trials, shared processing and testing infrastructure. FSSAI, the Department of Biotechnology, the World Bank and WFP took part.
key_quote: much of the school-feeding budget operates at under 10 rupees per student each day
vietnam_or_sea_focus: India only. A transfer model for Vietnam's upland child protein gap (Part III ch11.2).
demand_relevance: High. Treats a public feeding scheme as a protein-quality and cost buyer, not a meat-displacement channel.
notes: Trade press report of the roundtable; the organisers' own summary was not read.

actor: Bezos Earth Fund and the Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein at NUS
stated_interests: USD 30 million centre (September 2024) on microalgae and biomass fermentation, cultivated and plant-based proteins and hybrids; platforms for nutrition in Asian populations, safety and consumer acceptance. With Enterprise Singapore, up to SGD 1 million per growth-stage startup at TRL 7 to 9 (January 2026 call), for 'technical and commercial viability'. Example project: tofu by-product into protein.
key_quote: Asia is pivotal to the future of sustainable proteins, and Singapore is leading the way.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Targets East and Southeast Asia's 2.3 billion consumers. Vietnam not named.
demand_relevance: Medium. Runs consumer-acceptance research and wants products matching meat 'in both taste and price'; a natural partner for Vietnamese sensory and label tests.

stated_interests: Up to USD 300,000 including USD 75,000 in kind for early-stage plant-based, fermentation and cultivated startups; 100+ startups supported.
key_quote: 100+ startups transforming the food system
vietnam_or_sea_focus: No Asia programme or Vietnamese portfolio company found. Part II ch08 and app-s11 list it as a regional option.
demand_relevance: Low. No published demand evidence standard.

stated_interests: Asia Protein Buyers 100 benchmark (February 2026): 100 listed retailers, manufacturers, restaurant chains and hotel groups in 12 markets, 40 indicators. Protein diversification indicators: alternative proteins in strategy, 2030 sourcing targets, disclosure of alternative protein as a share of protein sales, reporting on the GFI and FAIRR framework. Asia Protein Transition Platform with 40+ companies and investor signatories.
key_quote: Diversify further with alternative proteins, setting a sales target to help drive uptake and scale.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Vietnam included: five buyers assessed (Vinamilk, Masan, Vinh Hoan, Minh Phu, Nam Viet); Vinamilk in Tier 3. Platform engagement named in China, Thailand, India, Japan and Singapore, not Vietnam.
demand_relevance: High. Defines corporate demand evidence as targets and disclosed volumes. Protein diversification averaged 7.4%; 48 of 100 buyers offer plant-protein products; only 2 publish sourcing targets and report volumes.

stated_interests: Protein diversification engagement (phase 2 ended October 2025; 73 investors with USD 11.5 trillion; 20 large manufacturers and retailers, none Asian). Coller FAIRR Protein Producer Index scores listed producers on alternative proteins.
key_quote: (Vinamilk) lacks a timebound target for protein diversification
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Vinamilk assessed in the 2024 index: rank 34 of 60, alternative proteins score 45 of 100, plant-based 1.30% of its product range.
demand_relevance: Medium. Investor pressure through disclosure; Asian coverage is via the producer index, not the engagement.

actor: Humane World for Animals (formerly Humane Society International)
country_or_region: United States; global, with a Viet Nam office
stated_interests: In Viet Nam: dog and cat meat trade, wildlife, cage-free hens (90,000 hens in 2024), disasters. Globally: Forward Food chef training and plant-based menu commitments; in 2025 new commitments to transition 2.3 million meals a year to plant-based and training of 370+ chefs and 570+ nutritionists in seven countries including Viet Nam.
key_quote: trained over 370 chefs, as well as more than 570 nutritionists and other professionals across Brazil, Canada, India, South Africa, Thailand, the UK and Viet Nam
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Active in Viet Nam. The Viet Nam page lists no plant-based programme and Forward Food lists no Viet Nam location, but the 2025 summary includes Viet Nam in plant-based training.
demand_relevance: Medium. Measures meals shifted; the one international diet-change implementer with staff in Vietnam that we found.
notes: Corrects the wave-6 note (CHY-63) that it has no plant-based work in Vietnam; the Viet Nam detail is not published.

stated_interests: Corporate sourcing policies in Asia: 175+ commitments by early 2025 (cage-free, improved production, plant-based); hotel plant-based menu targets in China (IHG Greater China 30% by 2025, Orange Hotels 70% across 750 hotels); claims 29 million corporate meals shifted to plant-based. In 2026 expanded plant-based policy work to India and Thailand, 'shifting protein procurement ratios' with hotels, foodservice and retailers.
key_quote: Our role isn't to introduce a new way of eating; it's to help institutions formalise and expand something that's already culturally present
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Hong Kong, China, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Korea, India, Thailand. Vietnam not named.
demand_relevance: High. Shows the corporate-commitment route working in Asian hospitality; measures meals shifted. Accor's own policy (50% vegetarian or plant-based dishes by 2030 in all hotels) already covers its 43 Vietnamese hotels.
notes: Lever figures are organisation claims reported by trade press.

actor: Animal Charity Evaluators and its recommended diet-change charities (Sinergia Animal, Good Food Fund)
stated_interests: 2025 recommendations include Sinergia Animal (institutional meat reduction in schools and universities; 998,000 meals replaced in 2023 across Argentina, Colombia and Indonesia) and Good Food Fund (China; certifies institutions at least 60% plant-based). Movement Grants fund smaller groups.
key_quote: 3.4 meals replaced per dollar (ACE estimate for Sinergia's institutional programme)
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Asian diet-change work in China, Indonesia and Thailand only. No Vietnamese grantee in the July 2025 Movement Grants round.
demand_relevance: High for metrics. Allocates on cost per meal replaced and suffering averted, units Part III does not report.

actor: Animal Alliance Asia (ReRoot Asia Fund, supported by Stray Dog Institute)
stated_interests: 2026 fund for 'projects that will bring diet change', including institutional menu offerings, through local advocates.
key_quote: transform individual food choices or institutional menu offerings
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Eligible countries in 2026: Taiwan, Philippines, Indonesia, Nepal, Pakistan, Japan. Vietnam not eligible.
demand_relevance: Medium. Would fund institutional menu work of the kind Part III proposes, but not in Vietnam.

actor: Giving Green and Founders Pledge (climate recommenders)
stated_interests: Giving Green's 2025 to 2026 top climate nonprofits include GFI, for public R&D funding, fair labelling and cultivated-meat market access. Founders Pledge Climate Fund impact page shows only energy-policy grants.
key_quote: Livestock production is responsible for at least 10% of global emissions
vietnam_or_sea_focus: None found for Southeast Asia or Vietnam food work.
demand_relevance: Low to Medium. A climate case needs tonnes of CO2e avoided per USD, which Part III does not give.
notes: Founders Pledge result is a clean negative from one page.

actor: Rockefeller Foundation (school meals) and the School Meals Coalition
stated_interests: USD 100 million pledge (March 2025) towards nutritious school meals for 100 million children; climate-conscious and regenerative school meals linked to public procurement; School Meals Coalition membership and financing initiatives.
key_quote: connecting local farmers practicing regenerative agriculture with public procurement systems
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Vietnam not named in the school meals work. Vietnam not listed among School Meals Coalition members, while Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Philippines, Thailand and Timor-Leste are.
demand_relevance: Medium. School-meal procurement is a demand lever, but these funders favour local and regenerative sourcing, not novel protein.
notes: Negative findings from the pages read.

stated_interests: Retailer methodology (November 2025) for measuring the ratio of plant to animal protein-rich food sales by weight, towards 60% plant; counts legumes, tofu, tempeh, seitan and meat alternatives; designed for countries where animal food intake exceeds health recommendations.
key_quote: This methodology is for retailers in countries where consumption of animal-based food exceeds health recommendations and planetary boundaries.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Global. WWF-Viet Nam's home page shows no diets or protein work.
demand_relevance: Medium. Offers the metric a Vietnamese retailer ratio target would likely use; weight-based, so tofu and low-protein chay would count fully.

stated_interests: Pagoda-based programme with Phap Van Pagoda: film screenings, plant-based cooking classes, dharma talks, free plant-based lunches, a donation-based vegan restaurant; plans to expand to the centre and south.
key_quote: convert[ing] five restaurants into going vegan, including a dog meat restaurant
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Vietnam-specific; aims at 15,000 pagodas and about 60 million lay Buddhists (organisation's framing).
demand_relevance: Medium. The only organised attempt we found to add chay or vegan occasions through pagodas; no measured outcomes or dates.

stated_interests: Tracks company animal welfare (cage-free egg) pledges in Vietnam and publicises inaction.
key_quote: We hold food companies accountable for their animal welfare commitments
demand_relevance: Low for protein. Shows that a commitments-tracking capacity exists that could extend to protein commitments.

actor: School-meal field-builders in Vietnam: Ajinomoto Vietnam with NIN and MOET; MOET, NIN and TH Group model scaled by Decision 973/QĐ-TTg
stated_interests: Ajinomoto, NIN and MOET School Meal Project: 120+ balanced menus, 360+ dishes, nutrition education. MOET, NIN and TH Group school meal model: 400 standard menus and one carton of fresh milk a day, piloted in 10 provinces in 2020 to 2021, now to be scaled nationally under the School Health Programme 2026 to 2035 (Decision 973/QĐ-TTg, 1 June 2026), which targets food-safety and nutrition management in all schools serving meals by 2030.
key_quote: Nhân rộng mô hình bữa ăn học đường đảm bảo dinh dưỡng hợp lý (scale up school meal models ensuring balanced nutrition)
demand_relevance: High. Menu templates decide which protein dishes public schools serve; both templates are built with a food company and one includes daily dairy.
notes: Corporate field-builders rather than funders; also relevant to the incumbents group. School counts using each menu set were not published on the pages read.

actor: Temasek and Nurasa (Asia Sustainable Foods Platform)
stated_interests: ASFP (2021) set up to commercialise sustainable foods in Asia through pilot infrastructure (FTIC; ScaleUp Bio JV with ADM; CREMER JV for plant protein) and investments. In Sep 2025 Nurasa co-developed Q Protein, soy-enhanced beef and chicken sold through a meat importer's retail channels in Singapore. The Temasek Review 2025 briefing says nothing on food.
key_quote: Our TPCs also see opportunities to invest in Southeast Asia, such as in Vietnam and Malaysia. (Temasek Review 2025; not about food)
demand_relevance: High for the blend route (TPP-03): the Temasek food arm now backs protein-enhanced meat inside a meat brand, not a stand-alone analogue. Would need a Vietnamese processor partner and blend acceptance data.
notes: A 2020 Temasek article on consumer-led demand was found but not used (pre-2024). A DealStreetAsia headline tags Nurasa with Growthwell (Jul 2026) but is paywalled and not used as a fact.

stated_interests: Invests in alternative proteins, ingredients, fats, sweeteners, flavourings and new crops; accelerator ticket USD 200,000 (125,000 cash, 75,000 in kind), follow-on up to USD 2.5 to 3.5 million; cohorts every January and July; asks for a minimum viable product.
key_quote: Minimum Viable Product in the alternative protein, ingredients or new crops space
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Singapore programme; no Vietnam mention on its 2026 site
demand_relevance: Medium: the realistic seed route for a Vietnamese ingredient founder; its entry bar is product, not market proof, so demand evidence matters more at follow-on.
notes: Package INV-018 records a 2021 statement that Vietnam was a target market; not re-verified. Latest dated portfolio item is December 2025.

stated_interests: Global report 2026: agrifoodtech funding USD 16.2 billion in 2025; capital directed to companies with real unit economics and paths to revenue. Invests in Green Rebel (Southeast Asian, locally inspired meat alternatives) and Meatiply (B2B co-development with manufacturers). No Asia-Pacific report after the 2024 edition.
key_quote: Investors are writing checks more selectively, directing capital towards companies with tangible science, real unit economics, and clear paths to revenue.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Southeast Asia portfolio; no Vietnam deal found
demand_relevance: High: its screen (unit economics, path to revenue) is exactly what Part III does not quantify for its target product profiles.
notes: Clean negative: no AgFunder Asia-Pacific agrifoodtech report for 2025 or 2026 on the research index (25 Sep 2026).

stated_interests: Backs early-stage Asia-Pacific food and alternative-protein startups; says investors want stronger fundamentals, diligence is longer and valuations lower (2023); thesis that Asia will become the manufacturing base for alternative protein (2022); avoids locally focused brands that cannot scale regionally.
key_quote: investors are looking for companies with stronger fundamentals
demand_relevance: High: a Vietnam-only chay ingredient business may fail its regional-scale test; it would ask for evidence of regional or export buyers.
notes: No 2024 to 2026 statement retrieved; package INV-019 lists portfolio (Green Rebel, TiNDLE, Meatiply).

type: Southeast Asian venture capital and multi-strategy manager
stated_interests: Backed Nutrition Technologies (insect feed made in Johor, sold across Asia including Vietnam) because it delivers at scale at a globally competitive price. We found no food-protein deal.
key_quote: Nutrition Technologies has led the way in delivering black soldier fly solutions at scale and at a price that is competitive on the global markets.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Southeast Asia; Vietnam is a customer market of its portfolio company
demand_relevance: Medium: revealed preference for B2B feed ingredients priced against incumbents; insect is a benchmark only in this package.
notes: Statement is from 2022; no 2024 to 2026 food statement found.

actor: Do Ventures (Vietnam Innovation and Private Capital Report, with NIC and VPCA)
type: Vietnamese venture capital and report publisher
stated_interests: Tracks Vietnamese private capital: USD 4.5 billion across 149 deals and USD 509 million of venture capital in 2025; AI funding up 13 times from 2023 to 2025; says capital is available for stronger founders with clearer unit economics. No food or protein theme on the report page.
key_quote: capital is still available, but investors are concentrating on stronger founders, clearer unit economics, and more mature opportunities.
demand_relevance: High: sets the evidence bar a Vietnamese protein venture must clear; no alternative-protein deal in its data.
notes: Package CAP-21 records agriculture at about USD 1 million of 2025 venture capital.

actor: VinaCapital Ventures (and HCM VIF, which VinaCapital operates)
type: venture capital arm; manager of a public-private city venture fund
stated_interests: Invested in INNOHAS (Korean plant-based OEM) in July 2024 to bring its products to Vietnam and Southeast Asia. VinaCapital is founding shareholder and operating unit of the VND 500 billion HCM VIF (Series A and B; core technology, green solutions; biotechnology among 2035 sectors); Hoang Duc Trung, the VinaCapital partner quoted on INNOHAS, is its CEO; about 50 proposals; 1 to 2 investments planned in Q4 2026.
key_quote: We are proud to invest in INNOHAS and help them introduce their healthy and delicious products to Vietnam.
demand_relevance: High: the only Vietnamese VC with a plant-based deal now steers the largest new public-private fund; its INNOHAS thesis (localised OEM products) shows no Vietnam launch two years on.
notes: Package notes INNOHAS's site did not mention Vietnam on 23 Sep 2026.

stated_interests: Growth capital in large minority stakes; sectors consumer, education, healthcare, biotechnology and agricultural technology; led Entobel's USD 25 million round (2022) with a seafood exporter as customer; 2025 to 2026 activity is listings of consumer and finance holdings.
key_quote: primarily a growth capital firm specializing in large minority investments
demand_relevance: High: the Entobel template (B2B product, named anchor buyer) is what it backs; it would need revenue scale and offtake, not surveys.
notes: No 2024 to 2026 food-protein deal found.

stated_interests: Co-invested USD 2.5 million in Entobel (2023, package); latest alternative-protein rationale found (ProNuvo, 2024) cites a USD 11 billion aquafeed and pet-food opportunity, lower footprint and circularity. We found no 2024 to 2026 Vietnam alternative-protein statement.
key_quote: (none demand-specific found)
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Global; Vietnam precedent is Entobel only
demand_relevance: Medium: needs an anchor feed buyer and a competitiveness case; the insect sector's 2024 to 2025 failures raise the bar.
notes: Feed, not food. Insect is a benchmark only.

stated_interests: Sustainable Agriculture and Food is one of six sectors; expects 80% of investments to have strong climate impact, 75% strong female participation and 100% to crowd in capital. 2025 to 2026 news covers energy and fintech.
key_quote: 80% of the investments are expected to have a strong climate mitigation and/or adaptation impact
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Emerging Asia; no Vietnamese agrifood deal (package)
demand_relevance: High: its impact tests make meat or emissions displaced per tonne decisive; by Part III's own model import substitution displaces no meat.
notes: Ticket USD 0.1 to 4 million per package CAP-45.

stated_interests: Strategy 2030 (Nov 2024) grows pet care, frozen, culinary and ingredients; alternative proteins sit in the third pillar, exploring new frontiers.
key_quote: new technologies and ideas like new aquaculture ecosystems or alternative proteins
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Southeast Asia; no Vietnam alternative-protein activity found
demand_relevance: Medium: a regional strategic that has moved alternative protein out of its growth pillars narrows the trade-sale exit the supply chapters assume.
notes: Status of its 2019 venture fund in 2024 to 2026 not found.

type: corporate incumbent with alternative-protein brand and partnerships
stated_interests: Launched Meat Zero and a cultured-meat partnership with Future Meat for Asian markets (2021 to 2022). In Vietnam, seven Meat Zero chay SKUs (minced, roast pork, bologna; 90 g to 1 kg) are listed on Kamereo, a B2B supplier to restaurants, cafes and hotels: 1 kg minced at VND 244,000, 200 g roast at VND 35,000.
key_quote: We are catching up with healthy food trend and nutrition foods in accordance with consumer needs (CPF, 2022)
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Vietnam (imported chay SKUs on a B2B platform)
demand_relevance: High: a regional incumbent sells analogues into Vietnam labelled chay through a HoReCa channel, competing with TPP-02 and TPP-04 and with any domestic textured-protein customer.
notes: Kamereo pages show metadata only: listing date, stock and protein content not visible. Part III launches_exits.csv LE-09 records Meat Zero as not found.

country_or_region: South Korea; Vietnam (CJ Foods Vietnam, CJ Cau Tre)
stated_interests: Co-invested in Shiok Meats (2021, package); sells bibigo chay dumplings in Vietnam (package LE-25); April 2026 partnership with Bach Hoa Xanh (2,700+ stores) to make bibigo a national brand; Vietnam sales about sevenfold since 2016 (company figure). No plant-based mention in 2026.
key_quote: will serve as an important stepping stone for Bibigo to become a 'national brand' in Vietnam
demand_relevance: Medium: buyer, co-packer or competitor for chay and plant-protein products; now concentrating on K-food volume through modern trade.
notes: Overlaps with the incumbents group; included here as a corporate investor.

country_or_region: Singapore HQ and R&D; sells in US and Europe
stated_interests: Raised a USD 100 million Series A (2022). In July 2025 its CEO said products were still 50% dearer than meat; in November 2025 it announced private label only from 2026 and the divestment of its US business and focused on Europe to cut marketing cost and improve unit economics.
key_quote: The fundamental issue is that there is no real underlying consumer demand to shift away from meat (co-founder Andre Menezes, 2025)
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Singapore base; no Vietnam; not selling in Southeast Asia in 2025
demand_relevance: High: a Singapore-founded scale-up abandoned the consumer-brand model for private label, the same logic Part III reaches for Vietnam.

stated_interests: Makes plant-based meat for regional dishes (rendang, satay) and grows through foodservice partners (Starbucks, IKEA, Domino's); raised USD 12.5 million (PPTI, Feb 2026) or USD 10.5 million (DealStreetAsia, Jan 2026) from existing backers; AgFunder is an investor.
key_quote: Foodservice partnerships have played a central role in the company's expansion
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Indonesia, Singapore; no Vietnam operations reported
demand_relevance: High: the one Southeast Asian plant-meat startup that raised in 2026 did so on foodservice volume and local cuisines, the model Part III recommends.
notes: Two amounts recorded; not averaged.

type: plant-based food maker with traditional vegetarian roots
stated_interests: Plant-based nutrition for Asian palates, 'accessible and affordable'; manufacturing in Johor since 1989 (Growth Well Industry) plus Singapore; own brands include traditional vegetarian lines; supplies chefs and F&B makers; sells in Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, Indonesia with planned Southeast Asian expansion.
key_quote: plant-based nutrition for Asian palates
demand_relevance: High: a regional analogue of a Vietnamese chay maker turned alternative-protein supplier; a competitor or partner for Vietnamese chay and textured-protein buyers.
notes: 2026 shareholder changes reported behind a paywall; not used.

stated_interests: Makes OEM and private-label products for food companies and retailers plus its own brand; claims 90% revenue growth in 2023 and profitability since 2021 (company claims); planned Vietnam and Southeast Asia products with local production after the VinaCapital investment (2024).
key_quote: (none demand-specific found)
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Vietnam planned (2024); no launch found by 2026
demand_relevance: Medium: shows the OEM model investors backed for Vietnam; the missing launch is itself a demand signal worth explaining.
notes: Package ECO-65 and VCO-31 cover the same deal.

actor: Avant Meats and Umami Bioworks (cultivated seafood; Vinh Hoan-linked)
stated_interests: Avant's Singapore unit declared voluntary winding-up in January 2026; the Hong Kong parent remains registered and sells Zellulin skincare peptides from fish cells. Umami Bioworks (merged with Shiok Meats in 2024) sells cultivated seafood as pet food (EU registration; Singapore launch, 2025) and signed a skincare and supplements partnership with Nippon Barrier Free (Japan) at the end of 2025. Vow, a comparator, moved to co-manufacturing in 2026.
key_quote: As the cultivated meat industry has evolved, so have we (Avant, Jan 2026)
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Singapore, Hong Kong, Japan; Vinh Hoan holds or held stakes; Minh Phu signed an MOU with Shiok (package)
demand_relevance: Medium: first revenues come from skincare and pet food, not seafood buyers; the Vietnamese exporters' options look stale.
notes: Vinh Hoan's current holdings not verified (Part III OQ-206).

actor: Angel Yeast, with its Vietnamese distributor ACC (Asia Ingredients Group)
type: Chinese yeast-protein maker and Vietnamese ingredient distributor
stated_interests: ACC and Angel Yeast held a seminar in May 2025 introducing yeast protein to Vietnamese food and nutrition makers for bakery, beverages, dairy and plant-based foods, with sampling and planned Innovation Days at customer sites.
key_quote: Yeast Protein as a breakthrough ingredient that supports product innovation and sustainable growth for the domestic food industry
demand_relevance: High: a novel fermentation protein from a Chinese incumbent is already being pushed into the Vietnamese buyers Part III names for TPP-06; no buyer, price or volume disclosed.
notes: Supplier, not a startup; included as the ingredient competitor Part III does not name.

actor: Vietnamese founder cohort: Emmay (Nam Tuoi Cuoi), VMEAT, Kashew, Ong Tempeh
stated_interests: Emmay: mushroom and mycelium foods (pate, banh mi filling, floss), 30+ products, 1.5 to 2 t a month, exports about 10% of revenue (UK, Australia, India, Netherlands); in 2022, 80% of revenue came from wholesale distribution and supermarkets. VMEAT (2021): 70% of revenue from F&B (its founders also run a chay noodle chain), over 90% of raw materials imported, VND 4 billion for 49% from two Shark Tank investors. Kashew: wholesale to restaurants, hotels, cafes and caterers. Ong Tempeh: founded 2023, Hanoi branch September 2025, sells to Sheraton, iVegan and restaurants and online.
key_quote: What we lacked were advisers ... in target import countries ... as well as the capital needed to execute our plans (Emmay founder, 2025)
demand_relevance: High: revealed founder channel choices (foodservice and wholesale first, exports small, imported inputs) that Part III does not use; these are the domestic deal pipeline investors would see.
notes: Company-reported figures. ThinkZone hosted Emmay's 2021 pitch (package CAP-15); outcome unknown. We found no sign of VMEAT activity after 2022 (package).

type: Listed dairy and plant-milk maker; also chilled beef (Vinabeef, a joint venture with Sojitz)
country_or_region: Vietnam; exports and subsidiaries in Cambodia and Laos
stated_interests: Premium high-protein, low-sugar, lactose-free adult nutrition; plant milk as a health solution; traceability and label compliance; Net Zero 2050; 2025 launches oat milk and two plant yoghurts; high-protein dairy (Green Farm Cao Đạm); beef
key_quote: "sữa thực vật không còn được xem là sản phẩm thay thế sữa động vật, mà đang được định vị như một giải pháp dinh dưỡng hỗ trợ các mục tiêu sức khỏe cụ thể" (AR 2025)
demand_relevance: High: only large confirmed buyer of a non-soy isolate (pea); also promotes dairy protein as more absorbable than plant protein
notes: Supplier criteria: price competitiveness, quality, standards; geographic diversification of supply. No plant-protein or protein-diversification target.

type: Listed sugar and soy-milk group; integrated soybean breeding
country_or_region: Vietnam; exports to Japan, Korea, US, Taiwan
stated_interests: Plant nutrition brand (soy and seeds); renew core soy milk; expand into new categories; invest in soybean sourcing areas; exports; school soy-milk donations

actor: Ministry of Health (MOH), incl. Department of Disease Prevention and Vietnam Food Administration
stated_interests: Nutrition Strategy targets (stunting below 15% by 2030; overweight caps; salt below 7 g a day); school-meal nutrition guidance; shift-meal and disease-prevention nutrition guidance; front-of-pack labelling; lead drafter of the Food Safety Law revision.
key_quote: School meals: animal protein 'ít nhất 4 - 5 ngày trong tuần, xen kẽ đạm có nguồn gốc thực vật (đậu các loại, đậu phụ) ít nhất 2 lần mỗi tuần' (animal protein at least 4 to 5 days a week, alternating with plant protein, legumes and tofu, at least twice a week).
demand_relevance: High. Sets the rules that decide whether plant or blended protein can enter school and shift meals and how products are labelled. Has already written a plant-protein slot into school guidance (Dec 2025) and adult guidance (Jul 2026). Needs cost, protein-quality and micronutrient evidence on specific products, not consumer attitudes.
source_ids: APR-01; APR-04; APR-16; APR-17; APR-07; APR-08
notes: No MOH document we read names alternative, novel or plant-based protein products; guidance names legumes and tofu only. Food Safety Law vote now May 2027.

actor: National Institute of Nutrition (NIN, Vien Dinh duong)
stated_interests: Recommended nutrient intakes (Decision 116/QD-VDD, 12 Feb 2026); Ten tips to 2030; food composition tables; school-meal guidance and menu tools; national nutrition surveys; SHiFT and BDN strategic partner; industry MoUs for research and communication.
key_quote: Ten tips, tip 3: 'nên ăn cá, thịt gia cầm và các loại hạt trong bữa ăn hằng ngày; ăn có mức độ các loại thịt đỏ' (eat fish, poultry and nuts, seeds and legumes daily; eat red meat in moderation).
demand_relevance: High. The technical gatekeeper for any nutrition claim, menu inclusion or food composition entry. Would need protein quality (DIAAS), iron and zinc bioavailability and composition data for Vietnamese dishes before endorsing a plant or blended product for children.
source_ids: APR-17; APR-16; APR-04; APR-23; APR-24; APR-42; APR-18
notes: Still cites 2020 survey figures in September 2026; we found no newer national survey results. Signs MoUs with firms (for example a supplement distributor, Sep 2026), a model an alternative-protein firm could use.

actor: Ministry of Education and Training (MOET), with its school-meal partners
stated_interests: School Health Programme 2026 to 2035 (Decision 973/QD-TTg); unified national school nutrition menu; rules on ban tru meal organisation; food safety after the 2026 pork case; boarding and border-school lunches.
key_quote: Plans to 'xây dựng thực đơn dinh dưỡng thống nhất trên toàn quốc' (build a unified national nutrition menu).
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Viet Nam only; priority to remote and ethnic minority areas
demand_relevance: High. The buyer-side rule maker for about 15.5 million primary and lower secondary pupils (Part III figure). A unified menu and ban tru rules would fix formats, frequencies and cost norms for school protein. Ajinomoto's menu software (4,262 schools by 2023, company claim) is a practical gate for new ingredients.
source_ids: APR-12; APR-13; APR-06; APR-09; APR-41; APR-45
notes: Decision 973 text itself not read (news report). Ajinomoto School Meal Project recorded here as a MOET partner, not as a separate actor.

stated_interests: Lead of the National Action Plan on Food Systems Transformation (Decision 300); FST Partnership (47 partners, Oct 2024) and International Support Group; provincial FST pilots; livestock strategy (58 to 62 kg meat per person by 2030); methane cap; food safety of primary products.
key_quote: Decision 300 task 5(a): 'Xây dựng và theo dõi bảng cân đối thực phẩm cấp quốc gia, cấp vùng, cấp tỉnh' (build and monitor food balance sheets at national, regional and provincial level).
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Viet Nam; Mekong Delta and northern uplands pilots
demand_relevance: Medium. MAE's stated goals are supply-side (more meat, lower emissions per unit, exports). It would use demand evidence to size the food balance sheets and to judge whether protein diversification belongs in the NAP-FST M&E. Its livestock targets pull against MOH's advice to moderate red meat.
source_ids: APR-02; APR-03; APR-10; APR-25; APR-23; APR-30
notes: Decision 300 contains no protein, meat or plant-protein target in the parts read.

actor: Politburo, National Assembly and Government (cross-cutting resolutions, laws and fiscal decisions)
stated_interests: Resolution 72 (health, 9 Sep 2025); Resolution 71 (education, 22 Aug 2025) requiring legal rules on school nutrition; Law on Disease Prevention 114/2025/QH15 (in force 1 Jul 2026); Food Safety Law revision (first reading Oct 2026, vote May 2027); excise on sugary drinks from 2027 (Law 66/2025/QH15); border-commune lunch support (Decree 339/2025).
key_quote: Resolution 72: nutrition must ensure 'cân đối về khẩu phần, thành phần dinh dưỡng, chất lượng bữa ăn, phù hợp với thể trạng, văn hóa và điều kiện kinh tế của người Việt Nam' (balanced rations and meal quality suited to Vietnamese physique, culture and economic conditions).
demand_relevance: High for timing and scope: these instruments set the windows (Food Safety Law, school-nutrition rule, excise) in which demand evidence can be used. None names protein sources.
source_ids: APR-05; APR-06; APR-14; APR-15; APR-07; APR-19; APR-20; APR-22; APR-09
notes: Ministry of Finance's role (excise, lunch budgets) is recorded under this row.

stated_interests: Under the Nutrition Strategy: research, production, branding, trade promotion and market development for fortified and 'healthy' foods; food safety for its product groups until the new law; trade promotion.
key_quote: Decision 02 assigns MOIT to promote 'phát triển thị trường sản phẩm thực phẩm tăng cường bổ sung vi chất dinh dưỡng, thực phẩm lành mạnh' (market development for fortified and healthy foods).
demand_relevance: Low to Medium. Could treat protein-dense plant foods as 'healthy foods' for trade promotion, but no instrument or criteria were found. Dairy strategy (Decision 309) pushes 'school meals with fresh milk', a competing protein.
notes: Lead ministry of Decision 309 not verified.

stated_interests: Under the Nutrition Strategy: fund S&T tasks on nutrition and food suited to Vietnamese; national standards and labelling rules for foods and fortified products. Biotechnology and strategic-technology programmes (covered in the supply and futures chapters).
key_quote: Decision 02: MOST to 'tăng cường bố trí kinh phí, ngân sách thực hiện các nhiệm vụ khoa học và công nghệ về dinh dưỡng, thực phẩm' (increase funding for S&T tasks on nutrition and food).
demand_relevance: Low. We found no demand-side interest stated by MOST beyond standards and funding S&T on nutrition and food. Its demand question is whether a funded project has a named adopter.
notes: Web search budget ran out before MOST's 2026 programme documents could be checked.

actor: Provincial People's Committees and city departments (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Dong Thap, Son La, border provinces)
stated_interests: Fund and supervise school meals and school health plans; set meal ceilings; run food-safety departments; pilot provincial FST plans (Dong Thap, Son La); deliver border-commune lunch support.
key_quote: HCMC Food Safety Department (Sep 2026): not to let ban tru meals be interrupted for long, while tightening kitchen and supplier controls.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Viet Nam; stunting hotspots in northern uplands
demand_relevance: High for public-meal volume. Provinces buy and regulate the meals. They would need cost per meal, supplier documents and food-safety assurance for any new protein, and evidence that it improves protein or micronutrients per VND.
notes: Hanoi subsidy and ceilings already in Part III (CHN-28, CHN-29).

actor: Vietnamese food-systems research partners of the NAP-FST: VAAS, IPSARD (now ISPAE) and Can Tho University
stated_interests: SHiFT and BDN strategic partners (VAAS, IPSARD); FST training of trainers (Can Tho University); food-environment policy analysis (IPSARD co-authored Food-EPI); soil and crop databases (VAAS).
key_quote: SHiFT: Can Tho University staff 'have taken a strong interest in leading the rollout of the ToT program'.
demand_relevance: Medium. They shape the evidence base used by MAE and provinces for the NAP-FST. A protein-diversification indicator or legume value-chain study would need them. No stated interest in alternative protein found.
notes: HUST food technology not examined in this group (no primary page retrieved).

actor: CGIAR in Viet Nam: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT, IFPRI, ILRI (Better Diets and Nutrition; Sustainable Animal and Aquatic Foods; One Health)
stated_interests: Sustainable healthy diets through food systems transformation; food-environment policy (Food-EPI); provincial FST plans and M&E; food safety in pork chains (ILRI, FSTWG priorities 2026 to 2030).
key_quote: Food-EPI: '74% of indicators scored low or very low'; school food policies exist 'but most measures remain non-mandatory'.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Viet Nam is one of three BDN target countries
demand_relevance: Medium to High. Produces the diet and food-environment evidence Vietnamese ministries cite. Would want tested evidence on how public-meal standards and food environments shift protein choices. CIAT staff have published on the political economy of the protein transition (cited in Food-EPI).
notes: No CGIAR Viet Nam activity on alternative protein found.

stated_interests: Country Programming Framework support for green, low-emission, climate-resilient agrifood systems; technical support to the NAP-FST and the FST Partnership; food safety (FSTWG).
key_quote: FAO Representative Vinod Ahuja: the next five years 'will be decisive for the country's food system transformation'.
demand_relevance: Medium. FAO would care about protein diversification only through the NAP-FST lens (food balance sheets, healthy diets, emissions). Needs a measurable indicator and data, not product evidence.
notes: FAO CPF 2022 to 2026 document not read in this session.

stated_interests: Country Programme 2027 to 2031: child and adolescent nutrition; stunting (18% in 2023, 32% among ethnic minorities); overweight; school food and complementary food standards; marketing restrictions on unhealthy foods.
key_quote: CPD para 18: 'Preventive nutrition interventions will be prioritized through strengthened school food and complementary food standards, and marketing restrictions'.
demand_relevance: High for public meals. UNICEF will help write the school food standards that decide whether processed plant or blended proteins count as healthy. It would need micronutrient, sodium and processing-level data and cost-effectiveness against eggs and milk.
notes: No UNICEF document mentions plant or alternative protein.

stated_interests: NCD risk factors: sugary drinks, salt, tobacco, alcohol; health taxes (supported the 2025 excise on sugary drinks).
key_quote: WHO Representative Angela Pratt: taxes deliver a 'win-win' of lower consumption of harmful products and new revenue.
demand_relevance: Low to Medium. WHO's diet agenda in Viet Nam is fiscal and nutrient-based (sugar, salt). It would ask whether plant analogues and chay products add salt or sugar, and whether plant drinks fall under the sugary-drink excise.
notes: No WHO Viet Nam document on protein sources found.

stated_interests: Agrifood net zero (Recipe for a Livable Planet): middle-income countries to cut livestock and rice emissions; in Viet Nam, low-methane rice and carbon credits (1 million hectare programme); historic focus on stunting among ethnic minorities.
key_quote: Recipe: 'High-income countries can also shift subsidies away from high-emitting food sources'.
demand_relevance: Low. Current Viet Nam agrifood climate work is rice. Diet shift is framed for rich countries. A demand-side protein case would need a cost per tonne CO2e that beats rice and livestock measures.
notes: Recipe full report not read; press release only.

stated_interests: Food security and agrifood transformation: USD 40 billion 2022 to 2030; nutrition a quarter of new commitments (metadata); 'integrating nutrition and healthy diets' (Viet Nam Country Director, Jan 2026).
key_quote: ADB Viet Nam: transition requires 'integrating nutrition and healthy diets' alongside value chains and resilience.
demand_relevance: Medium. ADB can lend to nutrition-tagged value chains. It would need an investable chain (for example domestic soy or mung bean to tofu and textured protein for public meals) with offtake evidence.
notes: No ADB alternative-protein document found.

actor: European Union (Delegation to Viet Nam; DG INTPA; EVFTA)
stated_interests: Global Gateway (EUR 560 million for transport and clean energy, Mar 2026); green transition incl. ecological agriculture in the Mekong Delta; EVFTA trade preferences (covered in Part III ch17).
key_quote: Global Gateway package for 'sustainable transport and clean energy'.
demand_relevance: Low. No EU food or nutrition programme in Viet Nam found. Its demand relevance runs through EVFTA buyers (Part III ch17), not development finance.
notes: SWITCH-Asia food-consumption work found only as a 2022 regional webinar; not used.

stated_interests: Market access for US beef, dairy, whey proteins, soybeans and tree nuts; market intelligence (GAIN reports).
key_quote: Tree nut imports grew with 'rising demand for plant-based milk among younger consumers'.
demand_relevance: Low to Medium. USDA's interest is exports of animal and plant protein inputs. It tracks plant-milk demand because it lifts US almond sales. Would need volume trends, not policy.
notes: Package already uses GAIN reports for supply data.

stated_interests: Nutrition-sensitive agriculture, food safety and One Health; smallholder livestock (beef, goats, chicken); ethnic minority livelihoods.
key_quote: Priority to 'enhance human health and nutrition through research on integrated farming systems, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, food safety and One Health'.
demand_relevance: Low to Medium. Would fund legume or smallholder protein research only with a nutrition or livelihood outcome and a market; public meals in upland schools are a possible buyer.
notes: Plan year read is 2023 to 24; package says 23 ACIAR projects in Viet Nam, none on alternative protein.

actor: GAIN and the Global Diet Quality Project
stated_interests: Diet quality measurement (DQQ, with Gallup and Harvard); workforce nutrition; fortification; demand for underconsumed foods.
key_quote: Viet Nam DQQ: pulses eaten by 40% of adults and processed meats by 18% on the previous day (Dec 2021 to Jan 2022).
vietnam_or_sea_focus: No Viet Nam country programme found; Viet Nam covered by the DQQ
demand_relevance: Medium. The DQQ is a cheap, repeatable diet-tracking tool that could add a chay-day or plant-protein module. GAIN's workforce nutrition work matches the canteen channel but lists no Viet Nam activity.
notes: DQQ sample size and 2023 to 2024 rounds for Viet Nam not checked.

stated_interests: Every child a healthy school meal by 2030; regional summit (Siem Reap, Nov 2024). WFP: school meals and fortification globally.
key_quote: SEA summit aim: 'every child in Southeast Asia and beyond receives a healthy and nutritious school meal, every day, by 2030'.
vietnam_or_sea_focus: Viet Nam not a member; no current WFP Viet Nam country page found
demand_relevance: Low for now. No route for international school-meal finance or technical support to Viet Nam found. Would matter only if Viet Nam joins.
notes: Negative findings from web pages; could be confirmed by a call.
